narrative:
On August 24, 2026, the Karnataka High Court registered an overall hearing rate of 36.8%, with 1,117 cases heard out of 3,039 scheduled across 45 judges. This represents a continued downward trend in clearance efficiency from previous sessions, falling from 38.5% on August 20 (1,002 of 2,600 heard), 42.0% on August 19 (1,179 of 2,808 heard), and 43.3% on August 18 (1,170 of 2,701 heard). This dip occurred despite today's scheduled docket being the largest of the period.

Performance varied widely among individual benches. Justice T.P. Vivekananda in Hall 35 demonstrated strong efficiency, hearing 50 of 65 scheduled cases (76.9%), while Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 19 managed a high-volume docket, hearing 116 of 252 cases (46.0%). Conversely, Justice B. M. Shyam Prasad in Hall 6, faced with a massive docket, heard only 1 out of 268 cases in his largest list (0.4%) and 2 out of 115 in another (1.7%), although he cleared 32 of 55 cases (58.2%) in his intermediate list. Additionally, the bench of the Chief Justice & K.S. Hemalekha did not hear any of their 69 scheduled cases across two lists.

In terms of hearing stages, Orders represented the largest block with 1,203 scheduled cases, achieving a 33.4% conversion rate (402 heard). Final Hearings lagged at 21.6% (133 heard of 615), while Preliminary Hearings achieved a higher rate of 55.2% (127 heard of 230). By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated court business with 1,473 scheduled and 474 heard (32.2%), followed by Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) at 46.4% (195 of 420 heard), and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) at 28.2% (113 of 400 heard).
